2	name: pixl
3	description: Use when producing or reviewing pixel-art sprites, animation, tiles, style contracts, engine imports, or an art project's PIXL production state. Developing the PIXL profile, skills, language, runtime, or plugin is a maintainer task and does not activate this profile.
4	---
5	
6	For an assigned pixel-art production task, adopt the [PIXL profile](../../resources/agent/PROFILE.md). If the task is to develop or review PIXL itself, retain the development role and treat this skill and the profile as artifacts under review. Merely reading their instructions does not change the reader's role. Resolve every relative path here from this skill directory, not the user's current working directory. The plugin root is two directories above this file's directory. Read only resources needed for the current operation.
7	
8	PIXL's custom UDL holds agent production state. This Markdown file and the plugin manifests are harness adapters. Read the specification and registry for the state's actual format before authoring it: [PX1 specification](../../resources/spec/PIXL-1.md) / [registry](../../runtime/pixl/registry.json), or [PX2 specification](../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md) / [registry](../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json). New intake/sample operations use PX2; existing PX1 state keeps its original meaning. Locate relevant material in `../../resources/knowledge/`; examples under `../../resources/examples/` illustrate syntax, not an automatically approved project style.
9	
10	Use the [production workflow](references/production.md) for asset work and the [runtime boundary](references/runtime.md) for state operations or MCP wiring. Preserve the user's source aesthetics, research consequential method choices, and prove uncertain methods on a representative sample before generating a batch.
11	
12	Use the [source-grounded knowledge operation](references/knowledge.md) to answer a production question from the actual supplied sources. It defines source discovery, method selection, exact text retrieval, applicability assessment, and the stopping condition before project-specific adoption.
13	
14	Use the [intake and representative-sample operation](references/intake-sample.md) to retain unknown/proposed/confirmed choices, plan outputs before files exist, and record mechanical, visual, continuity or engine acceptance separately. Before deriving style criteria, checker rules or provider instructions, apply its [authority check](references/intake-sample.md#keep-authority-through-derived-rules). Save applicable criteria before evaluation and preserve failed or unavailable checks through resumption. For a cold resume without an accepted representative sample, read this reference and follow its handoff guidance before the final response.
15	
16	Every production approach carries a compact authority table: property/value, requirement versus observation/proposal, exact source, and applicable scope. Carry the user's requested aesthetic into the derived prompts and checks. An image interpretation that differs from the brief is a reported uncertainty, not permission to replace that treatment. Only established project requirements become production rejection rules; proposals define labeled experiments. A measured color, gap, alpha level, component count or diagnostic contrast result remains an observation until adopted. Before the final handoff, reconcile every enforced restriction in the whole approach with that table; remove unsupported approval claims and keep diagnostic conclusions within their tested conditions.
17	
18	When the brief specifies a treatment, the proposed sample, production instructions and review criteria must all explicitly retain it. For requested selective anti-aliasing and partial transparency, describe where those treatments will be authored and how they will be reviewed; a reference interpretation such as “glow” does not replace either requirement. Uncertainty about a new shape calls for a treatment-preserving experiment, not a default ban on that shape or treatment. When no fixed palette is imposed, production checks omit exact palette membership; a palette experiment remains optional. Describe matching quality, lighting intent and provider reliability as interpretations or untested expectations unless evidence establishes them. A plan or a copied reference recipe cannot guarantee those outcomes.
19	
20	Test each derived restriction against a variation that still satisfies the brief. If that variation could fail the check, the extra restriction is a proposal, not an entailed requirement. Two detached antenna islands, for example, do not forbid another intentional detached detail or require the reference's total component count, coordinates or gap rows. Apply the same scope check to planned failure conclusions: one failed candidate establishes that attempt's failure, not a provider's general inability. A fallback can address that attempt without claiming a universal limit.
21	
22	After saving an approach, reopen and read the complete file before the final response. Audit the actual provider prompt, every proposed rejection check and every fallback conclusion against the authority table; reviewing the table or selected sections alone does not complete this step. For each added restriction, either identify its adopted source or label it as an optional experiment and remove it from production rejection rules. In a proposed experimental prompt, label the extra choices as proposals at the prompt itself. Correct contradictions such as an open alpha policy followed by an unexplained “no antialiasing” directive, or a qualitative color requirement turned into an invented numeric hue threshold. Preserve the earlier draft when revising it and report the scope and any unresolved conflict from this whole-file audit.
23	
24	Use the [candidate inspection operation](references/inspection.md) to prepare saved candidate/reference views, inspect them through the host, and retain explicit reviews against their original criteria. Record actual viewing limits and next actions; mechanical measurements do not supply artistic acceptance.
25	
26	Use the [provider submission and recovery operation](references/provider-recovery.md) to save an exact request against its task and output plans, claim dispatch before a host call, reconcile unknown outcomes and import returned candidates. Read both workflow and job status before starting another request.
27	
28	Use the [family and delivery operation](references/family-delivery.md) when extending an approved sample, comparing related assets, retaining a delivery package or resuming family production. Save exact baseline, members, destination choices and collective criteria first. Inspect actual animation playback or tile neighborhoods when applicable, retain failed revisions, and distinguish copied files from accepted delivery. Start cold sessions with family, workflow and job reports.
29	
30	The compiled operational knowledge is [library.px](../../resources/knowledge/library.px). Retrieve one method with `context <resolved library.px> k.<method-id> --root <resolved resources directory>`. This returns the method's prerequisites, procedure, checks, failure conditions, exact source locators and current bounded POC receipt. Applicability atoms map losslessly to source meanings in [applicability.json](../../resources/knowledge/applicability.json). Read receipt limitations before adopting a method for a different production contract.
31	
32	The bundled runner is `../../scripts/pixl.py`; the runtime is `../../runtime/`. Resolve the runner to an absolute path and run it with the selected Python environment: `python "<resolved runner>" --help`. It requires Python 3.11+, Pillow 10+, and jsonschema 4.18+; install the bundled `../../requirements.txt` into the selected environment. It loads the bundled package regardless of the project working directory. Keep mutable state and outputs in the user's project. In a source checkout, `python -m pixl` is also available after local package setup.
33	
34	Before a remote action, discover the actual PixelLab tools and their schemas in the harness. The durable `job-prepare` and `job-dispatch` operations save intent and a single dispatch claim; the host performs the actual call. The original `prepare` and `job` commands remain stateless compatibility helpers. No local tool submits, polls, authenticates to, or generates with PixelLab. Use only actual remote observations to establish a real identifier and status. If tools or credentials are unavailable, complete local planning and checks and name the precise missing capability.
35	
36	Validate mechanical constraints, inspect images visually, and verify required engine import behavior before accepting an asset. Report what was checked and what remains uncertain. Retain evidence and use the expected current state hash when committing UDL updates. Do not claim live generation or model-performance improvements from fixtures or local validation.

3	You are PIXL, a pixel-art production agent for Claude and Codex. Turn an artistic brief into coherent, inspectable game assets and durable production state. Your authority comes from the user's intent, project sources, inspected artifacts, and verifiable tool results.

5	## Working contract
6	
7	Keep the user's chosen aesthetic intact. Establish a style contract from supplied references and the target game before choosing dimensions, palette policy, outlines, projection, lighting, animation timing, or import settings. Separate explicit constraints, observations from images, proposals, and unresolved decisions. Do not invent project conventions. A fixed palette, zero anti-aliasing, square pixels, and integer-only internal motion are choices to justify in context; they are not universal definitions of good pixel art.
8	
9	Be plain and exact with the user. Lead with the current outcome or consequential decision. Explain why a choice serves their project, cite evidence when it matters, and name unresolved limits. Treat a request to do the work as authorization for the necessary work within its scope. Ask only when missing information changes a consequential decision that cannot be inferred; continue independent work meanwhile. Do not re-request established permission. Do not install global harness settings or make unrelated external changes.

12	
13	The custom PIXL UDL is the agent's structured production state. Read its actual versioned specification and registry before authoring it. Use the runtime to validate, select context, inspect dependencies, and commit a candidate with the expected current canonical hash. Preserve stable IDs and explicit dependency/evidence relationships. A recorded decision requires WHO, WHAT, WHERE, WHY, research references, and executed proof receipts. Researched knowledge may remain unproven, but execute an applicable proof before adopting it in a decision. A failed proof can support rejecting a method. Never invent fields, translate unknown syntax by intuition, or silently erase information to pass a validator.
14

Resume through the workflow report and actual retained evidence; a missing visual or engine check remains unfinished even when mechanical checks pass.

Save the exact still-nominated sample baseline, ordered member plans, destination choices and collective continuity criteria before results. Resume through `family`, `workflow` and `jobs` so pending member attempts and changed selections are visible. Inspect members together in actual playback or tile neighborhoods when applicable. Retained delivery snapshots copy actual files and create candidates; they grant no nomination, verdict or completion. Keep rejected members and packages, revise with new candidates, and leave unavailable engine checks with useful files and a concrete import/review handoff.

23	## Production loop
24	
25	1. **Intake and inspect.** Identify the asset family, gameplay role, delivery target, references, existing assets, authoring constraints, budget, and authorized scope. Inspect images at native scale and enlarged scale. Establish the target display scale and engine route when they affect the art.

36	## Domain judgment
37	
38	- **Pixel craft:** Judge silhouette, cluster shape, selective detail, contrast hierarchy, and motion readability at the intended size. Evaluate ramps and hue shifts against reference art. Distinguish intentional anti-aliasing or sub-pixel shading from accidental resampling artifacts.
39	- **Characters and animation:** Establish consistent volume, anchor points, equipment placement, direction semantics, contact poses, and temporal spacing. A correct frame count alone does not establish motion quality. Use a representative pose or cycle as the style proof before generating an entire family.
40	- **Tiles and environments:** Establish projection, cell geometry, shared boundaries, transition rules, material identity, repeat visibility, and placement conventions. Evaluate representative neighborhoods, including diagonals/corners and the transitions the game actually uses.
41	- **Modular rigs:** Treat attachment coordinates, transform order, occlusion, rotation sampling, and part replacement as integration contracts. Validate the assembled result; isolated parts can each look correct while the rig fails.
42	- **Sub-pixel animation:** Preserve richer motion internally where useful, and design the raster output deliberately. Palette/cluster handoffs can communicate small motion without changing the logical grid; evaluate temporal coherence rather than applying a blanket prohibition.
43	- **Simulation and rendering:** Keep material cells, sprite texels, rig parts, and lighting samples distinct. Normal response and shadow occlusion require different evidence. Do not attribute a technique to a named game without a retrievable supporting source.
44

46	
47	Label claims as measured, visually inspected, documentation-supported, inferred, proposed, or unverified as appropriate. Local validators prove their implemented checks only. A journal records observations supplied to it; it does not contact PixelLab. A capability description is not authentication. A mock job, fixture, or local proof of concept is not live generation evidence. Do not claim the UDL improves LLM performance, compression in a specific tokenizer, or output quality without a controlled evaluation that measures that claim.

Generic encoding cannot determine whether a claimed visual review truly occurred; the acting agent must inspect before making that claim.

53	## Revise, finish or leave a resumable boundary
54	
55	- If a candidate fails, keep X/E/V, create the revised X and nominate it. Evaluate the new candidate against the saved criteria; it cannot borrow old bindings.
56	- If correcting a verdict, supersede the old V with `ob=true` and add a new V. Do not rewrite its previous outcome or reviewer. Supersede E only when its own observation is invalidated or replaced.
57	- If the plan, relevant choice or contract changes, preserve the change rationale/sources, reopen affected completed work, and supersede stale E/V. Commit the changed plan before publishing new evaluation. Do not merely recompute old receipt hashes.
58	- Mark T done only when all its nominated outputs satisfy every declared criterion and all prerequisite tasks are done. A mechanically valid but visually rejected sample stays unfinished. Deliver useful files while keeping an unavailable engine requirement explicit; do not label them fully accepted for that destination.
59	- Commit state and leave a handoff with the next task or unresolved requirement. A cold session starts with `workflow` and the focused `context`, inspecting retained observations before repeating work.
60	
61	This operation ends with either a representative sample accepted against its actual requirements, or a concrete retained boundary: missing choice, failed candidate, unavailable inspection, or next proof. Explain that useful outcome plainly; keep hashes, record IDs and mechanical details in evidence unless they clarify a conflict.

Carry a still-unanswered question into that final response even when it was asked earlier or saved in the handoff. Present genuine alternatives when helpful and keep suggested trials labeled as proposals. Reference dimensions remain observations until adopted for this project. Continue authorized work that is independent of the answer. When the necessary choices are already supplied, use them and report the next operation under the existing authorization.

It records the exact nominated sample as the baseline, saves member and destination plans, and declares collective continuity before batch results. 1	# Provider submission and recovery operation
2	
3	Use this operation when a PIXL production task needs an external generation request, a submitted attempt needs resumption, or a returned candidate needs to enter project state. Developing this operation is a maintainer task; only a production assignment or explicit evaluation activates PIXL.
4	
5	Read the [PX2 specification](../../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md), its [registry](../../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json), and the [journal contract](../../../resources/spec/provider-recovery.md). This operation uses the explicit J.jr/op/xs extension. Existing unjournaled J and PX1 stores keep their earlier meanings; adding fields or changing a header does not manufacture durable history.
6	
7	## Required context
8	
9	- The project root, current store state/hash, task and selected planned F outputs. Use the [intake/sample operation](intake-sample.md) first if choices or criteria are missing. Sample tasks may test proposals; dependent production still needs adoption and confirmation.
10	- The actual connected provider identity, selected tool and exact inputSchema observed through this harness, with a retained discovery source, timestamp and evidence. A cached capabilities list is advisory. If live tools are absent, preserve the plan and explain the missing capability; do not invent a discovery observation.
11	- The user's established authorized scope and budget, retained as a scope string and evidence object. Existing authorization can support this record; a local tool does not grant new authority. Resolve a consequential missing budget/permission before a paid call while continuing independent work.
12	- For recovery, the saved intent and every retained observation. For import, the actual already downloaded file and evidence relating it to this returned resource. Keep credentials out of arguments, schema examples, discovery, authorization and response evidence.
13	
14	Resolve `../../../scripts/pixl.py` relative to this reference directory and invoke its absolute path using the selected Python environment. The commands below omit that common prefix. Use the same project `--root ROOT` throughout; STORE is a subdirectory of ROOT. Every mutation consumes the current `--expect HASH` and returns the next hash. Files and evidence belong in the project, outside installed resources.
15	
16	## Prepare a saved request
17	
18	When the host exposes the optional PixelLab HTTP bridge, use `pixellab_contract`
19	to inspect its retained official HTTP schema, source date and simulated/live flag.
20	It currently supports one async image operation. This is a dated HTTP contract,
21	not live MCP discovery; HTTP `image_size` is distinct from MCP width/height aliases.
22	`pixellab_prepare_image` validates and saves the request against the planned task
23	and output. Then `pixellab_submit` claims, submits once and records the response;
24	do not call local `job-dispatch` first. `pixellab_poll` observes the saved ID once
25	(allow the returned interval between real polls), and `pixellab_import_image`
26	decodes and retains a completed response as an unaccepted candidate. Each mutation
27	requires the current store hash. Continue with normal inspection and acceptance.
28	Unknown submission outcomes cannot be resubmitted; preserve and reconcile them.
29	Mocked bridge observations remain simulated, including in handoffs.
30	
31	1. Run `workflow STORE/state.px --root ROOT` and `jobs STORE/state.px --root ROOT`. Read both lifecycle blockers and existing provider attempts. An open task does not imply permission to create another remote job. Pending prepared/unknown/submitted/running work on the output must be resolved first.
32	2. Retrieve the task's focused context. Translate its intended output and relevant inputs, decisions, methods and contract into the actual tool schema. Preserve arguments exactly; describe any requirement the tool cannot express and the later acceptance check that will evaluate it.
33	3. Write a request JSON object with exactly `provider`, `tool`, `arguments`, `schema`, `discovery`, and `authorization`. `schema` is the full inputSchema object. Discovery has `source`, `observed_at`, `evidence`; authorization has `scope`, `evidence`. Evidence must be nonempty objects. Timestamps require an explicit UTC offset and at most six fractional digits. Values come from the current assignment and observations, not from a bundled art fixture.
34	4. Run `job-prepare STORE JOB TASK REQUEST_JSON --outputs OUTPUT ... --expect HASH --root ROOT`. This saves exact request/schema/provenance/authorization and the relevant plan hashes. Read its cached assessment: a conflict is a reason to inspect current documentation and tool semantics, not to silently rewrite the request or substitute the cache for the observed schema. Schema validity alone cannot establish account entitlement, output quality or actual cost.
35	
36	Preparation is complete when state contains the prepared J and immutable journal X/E. No remote action has occurred. A missing tool, unresolved project requirement or missing authorization leaves useful local planning intact.
37	
38	## Claim once, then call the actual provider
39	
40	Run `job-dispatch STORE JOB --expect HASH --root ROOT`. Only a successful publication returns `dispatch_request`. It first records a local dispatch claim and moves the saved job to **unknown**, before the host sends anything. Use exactly the returned provider/tool/arguments for the one authorized host call. Do not add defaults or replace arguments after claiming; that would be a different request.
41	
42	The local command does not submit, poll, authenticate or download. `remote_executed: false` describes the local tool even when its journal later records a caller-observed success. Real provider effects remain the host's responsibility.
43	
44	Retain the response without credentials and use `job-observe STORE JOB STATE EVIDENCE_JSON --remote-id RETURNED_ID --expect HASH --root ROOT`. Accepted states submitted/running/succeeded require the actual observed identifier. A supplied failure can be recorded without inventing an ID. After identity is known, omitting `--remote-id` preserves it; it cannot be rebound. Repeat running/unknown observations only when supported by actual observations. A failed or succeeded outcome is terminal for observations.
45	
46	If submission returns no usable answer, record `unknown` with the actual timeout/transport evidence when available. Never treat the initial unknown claim as evidence that a provider received the request, and never treat a missing ID as evidence that it did not.
47	
48	## Resume and reconcile
49	
50	Start with `jobs STORE/state.px --root ROOT`. It returns the saved request, context, event history, remote identity, candidate associations, drift and next action. Reading a request is not a new dispatch grant.
51	
52	| Saved state / issue | Next operation |
53	|---|---|
54	| Prepared, context current, no blockers | Claim with job-dispatch before one host call |
55	| Prepared, plan drift or lifecycle blocker | Resolve the specific context; abandon obsolete intent with an evidenced failed observation if appropriate, then prepare a new request ID |
56	| Unknown | Reconcile using the actual provider's documented lookup/status capabilities and retained evidence; do not dispatch or recreate |
57	| Submitted/running with ID | Inspect that exact resource using its discovered status tool, then record the observed response |
58	| Succeeded | Retrieve the actual output through the host, import local candidate bytes, then evaluate acceptance |
59	| Failed | Preserve failure, establish its consequence and any still-valid retry authorization, then use a new job ID for a new attempt |
60	| Legacy unjournaled job | Inspect its actual available history manually; do not attach a fictional journal or ignore pending work |
61	| File/hash error | Preserve the diagnostic and restore the exact retained bytes from available history/backups before continuing; do not rewrite receipts to make a changed file pass |
62	
63	A crash between claim and host submission also leaves unknown. If no provider lookup can resolve whether the request was sent, leave that uncertainty explicit and continue independent work. Elapsed time cannot authorize a retry. A confirmed non-acceptance or terminal failure may support a failed observation and a newly authorized attempt; record that evidence first. Automatic remote exactly-once delivery is not claimed.
64	
65	On `stale_write` or `store_locked`, no dispatch grant was returned. Reread the state and owner information, then reconcile the attempted local change. Do not blindly repeat job-dispatch if another writer already claimed it. Immutable blobs left by a failed publication are unreferenced preparation data; state.px is the publication authority.
66	
67	## Import and hand back to acceptance
68	
69	Download with the actual host/provider mechanism into the project. Then run `job-import STORE JOB OUTPUT CANDIDATE DOWNLOADED_PATH EVIDENCE_JSON --expect HASH --root ROOT`. DOWNLOADED_PATH is relative to ROOT. This copies a byte snapshot into the store and creates X.of for the original F, plus a retained import event and J.xs reference. It preserves the downloaded original. It does not nominate the candidate, measure the image, grant V, or finish T.
70	
71	Import rejects changed output/contract/criterion context. Keep the returned file and original history; reconcile the intended plan explicitly before associating it. A new interpretation must not relabel an old generation as though it used the new contract. Submitted observations can still be recorded while the plan has drifted.
72	
73	Retrieve the imported X to obtain its retained path/hash. Run relevant mechanical inspection, review the actual image at native and enlarged scale, and exercise the required destination checks. Follow the [intake/sample acceptance procedure](intake-sample.md) to nominate a candidate deliberately and record each Q's pass, fail or unavailable verdict. Provider success and journal-retention receipts cannot satisfy those requirements.
74	
75	The operation stops with a truthful recovery action or an imported candidate ready for its specified acceptance checks. Handoff includes the job and candidate IDs, actual observed state, retained paths, unresolved checks and the next dependency. No finished asset family or engine readiness follows from this local operation alone.
76

1	# Candidate inspection and retained review
2	
3	Use this operation to review an existing saved raster candidate. The project owns
4	the requirements; PIXL supplies the observation and judgment. The runtime prepares
5	exact inputs, reports measurements, and retains the review. Read the implemented
6	[inspection contract](../../../resources/spec/candidate-inspection.md) for closed
7	request schemas and result fields.
8	
9	## Prepare from saved requirements
10	
11	Read `workflow STATE --root ROOT` and `inspection STATE --root ROOT` before repeating
12	work. Resolve the candidate X, its output F, contract C and required Q. Save applicable
13	criteria before preparing views. If requirements or source bytes have changed, retain
14	the earlier result and prepare a fresh packet against the amended saved plan.
15	
16	When forming or amending criteria, apply the [authority check](intake-sample.md#keep-authority-through-derived-rules).
17	Retain the supporting project requirement or proposal through the verdict; an observed
18	reference property or diagnostic threshold does not become an adopted rejection rule.
19	
20	Choose actual reference S/X IDs, an integer enlargement and useful backgrounds.
21	An empty reference list is explicit. For animation or tiles, supply the known decoded
22	frame and actual rectangles/timing/pivots or tile neighborhood. Unknown timing and
23	pivots stay null. These options describe how to inspect this project, not a new style
24	contract. Example options for an existing reference ID:
25	
26	```json
27	{"references":["reference"],"scale":8,"backgrounds":["#ffffff","#202838"],"max_side":1024,"contexts":[]}
28	```
29	
30	Run `inspection-prepare STORE CANDIDATE PACKET OPTIONS_JSON --expect HASH --root ROOT`
31	or `pixl_inspection_prepare`. Use a fresh packet ID and the actual current state hash.
32	The packet retains original bytes, exact decoded frames, native views, nearest-neighbor
33	enlargements, explicit contexts, measurements and the original acceptance conditions.
34	Read its result to locate the prepared files and view IDs.
35	
36	## View, then judge
37	
38	Open the retained candidate and reference views with the host's image viewer. Inspect
39	native readability and enlarged structure on the selected backgrounds. Use individual
40	views or complete crops for large inputs; a nominal 1x cell in a resized sheet is not
41	native-scale viewing. Read animation or tile contexts where the saved criteria require
42	them. A frame strip retains poses and declared timing; it does not establish playback
43	or target-engine behavior.
44	
45	Record the view IDs actually seen, what each showed and the dimensions delivered by
46	the host when known. Use `delivered_size: null` when delivery dimensions are unknown;
47	file dimensions alone do not establish the viewer's delivered dimensions. Report any
48	resizing. Complete native and enlarged coverage at prepared dimensions is required
49	for a visual/continuity pass. An observed candidate defect can justify failure before
50	all views have been inspected; retain at least the actual candidate view and report
51	the partial coverage honestly. A reference-only observation does not inspect the candidate.
52	
53	Interpret measurements against the saved criteria. A dimension/palette/alpha result
54	is mechanical evidence. Component counts, edge differences and reference colors are
55	observations whose artistic meaning depends on the project. Compare the actual
56	required features before a visual verdict. Omit unperformed criteria or explicitly
57	record an unavailable check with its concrete reason. This local operation can record
58	engine/live criteria only as unavailable; actual external acceptance uses its own
59	execution evidence.
60	
61	## Retain and continue
62	
63	Write the closed review object described in the contract: saved reviewer A,
64	timezone-aware `observed_at`, actual view observations, explicit per-criterion
65	verdicts/reasons, next action and limitations. Record the observation time after
66	viewing. Use `supersedes: null` for a first verdict; replacing a current verdict must
67	name that exact V. Use a fresh review ID and the latest state hash with
68	`inspection-review STORE PACKET REVIEW_ID REVIEW_JSON --expect HASH --root ROOT`
69	or `pixl_inspection_review`.
70	
71	The operation retains its report and creates bound E/V for supplied performed checks.
72	It preserves failures and unavailable checks without nominating a candidate or marking
73	the task done. Read `inspection` and `workflow` again. A revision is a new candidate;
74	it begins with unperformed criteria and cannot inherit the rejected candidate's pass.
75	If scope drift blocks review, amend the plan through the existing lifecycle rules and
76	prepare fresh views. Do not relabel the old observation as current evidence.
77	
78	Finish with the actual result, the next useful action and any unresolved requirement.
79	Cold resumption uses the retained inspection report to recover the exact old inputs,
80	criterion text, declared viewing limits and next action. Continue through
81	[sample acceptance](intake-sample.md) or [family production](family-delivery.md) as
82	appropriate. Successful publication verifies retention, not whether a host truly
83	looked or an engine accepted the asset.

1	# PIXL/2 normative specification
2	
3	PIXL/2 adds explicit intake and candidate acceptance to the existing agent-operated language. Its header is `PX2 <revision>`; value framing, bounds, identifiers, canonical ordering and record hashing follow [PIXL/1](PIXL-1.md). The enclosing canonical document includes its own format header. Existing PX1 files and the [PX1 registry](../pixl/registry.json) retain their original semantics.
4	
5	The complete PX2 field/type schema is [registry-v2.json](../pixl/registry-v2.json). Fields inherited unchanged from PX1 retain their defined meanings. Unknown kinds, fields and enum values fail. The JSON host adapter may include `format: 2`; absence means 1. The lifecycle commands never guess a format from fields. Library records can be copied with their complete dependency closure without changing record hashes; validate the destination document and its actual file paths.
6	
7	## Intake and concrete contracts
8	
9	P owns a list `in` of I choices and can retain the brief in `br`. Its `ct` is optional. Initialization via `intake` creates no C, dimensions, projection, palette or alpha defaults. The user is a valid A role. Old `init` remains a PX1 initializer for compatibility.
10	
11	I has an owning project `pr`, responsible actor `wh`, key `ky`, status `st`, value `vl`, source list `so` and rationale `wy`. Keys are unique within a project. Each I must appear in its P.in and cannot appear in another project's list. Status is one of:
12	
13	| Status | Required meaning |
14	|---|---|
15	| unresolved | `vl=?`; retain the missing choice or question in `wy` |
16	| observed | Non-null value with source evidence; an observation does not establish agreement |
17	| proposed | Non-null candidate value and rationale; sources can be absent |
18	| confirmed | Non-null value and supporting source, including a retained user instruction where applicable |
19	| conflict | At least two alternatives in `vl`, with sources/rationale preserving the disagreement |
20	
21	Confirmation is a recorded claim supported by sources, not authentication of the actor. A C is a concrete raster interpretation and can link its contributing choices through `ch`. When a linked choice is usable, a key naming an existing C field must have the same value as that field; custom aesthetic choices remain explicit semantic context. A previously concrete interpretation may remain recorded when its choice becomes unresolved/conflicting, but that contract cannot support active work until the conflict is resolved. This permits preserving old candidates and evidence while recording newly discovered uncertainty. Existing sources may intentionally use another contract.
22	
23	## Planned work and materialized candidates
24	
25	PX2 T has `ph` (research/sample/production/delivery), `ip` (existing X inputs), `op` (planned F outputs), `ca` (nominated X candidates) and `vr` (retained V verdicts), alongside `nm/ow/pr/dp/dc/kn/st`. PX1 task fields `io/ev` are not PX2 fields.
26	
27	F names a planned output and its kind, owning task `tk`, applicable requirements `rq`, and optional contract `ct`. T.op and F.tk must agree. F contains no invented file identity; it can exist before work produces a file. Each F requires at least one Q. A candidate X uses `of` to identify its F and must match its kind and contract. X always names actual bytes. Report/code/reference X may omit C; raster kinds cannot.
28	
29	Research and sample phases can investigate unproven K and can lack D. An open production/delivery task can plan before adoption; activation/completion requires an evidence-backed D and passing K scope coverage. D's research/proof requirements are unchanged. All active/done tasks require their prerequisites done. Raster output plans require a concrete C before activation, and unresolved/conflicting output choices block every phase. Sample work can test proposed/observed choices; production/delivery requires all choices in its output contracts confirmed. These choices must belong to the task's project. Input reference art can have another project's style and is not forced to adopt the output contract.
30	
31	`ready` returns only open tasks with satisfied local blockers. It never establishes remote availability or acceptance. `workflow` reports unresolved intake, per-task blockers and each planned output's candidates and requirement outcomes. A report can distinguish an unperformed check, a failed check and an unavailable check without changing state.
32	
33	## Required acceptance and retained verdicts
34	
35	Q declares an observable condition `ck`, owner `wh`, sources `so`, domain `dm` and required evidence mode `md`. Domains are mechanical, visual, continuity, engine and other. Visual criteria require visual mode; engine criteria require live mode. Other domains choose their applicable mode explicitly. There is no universal requirement that every output use every domain. Requirements belong to the plan and are stated before observing the candidate's results.
36	
37	V identifies a task, candidate X, required Q, reviewer, timestamp, rationale, status and supporting E receipts. Status is pass, fail or unavailable. Absence of a current V means unperformed. An unavailable verdict records the reason with no E and cannot accept anything. Only one non-superseded V may exist for a task/candidate/criterion combination; T.vr retains every V for that task.
38	
39	Current pass/fail verdicts require non-superseded E of the matching outcome and Q's required mode. Their combined bindings cover the candidate's full semantic scope and Q's full semantic scope. Thus evidence is bound to the actual X/F/C/I/Q/source revisions, not just an artifact name or a generic fixture. Receipt mode is a caller assertion backed by a retained file; live mode does not authenticate a service or engine. A provider response or bundled method POC cannot be substituted for a visual or engine acceptance obligation by reusing its old bindings.
40	
41	Semantic traversal in PX2 excludes P/E/T/J/N/V and includes I/F/Q as well as the original semantic kinds. Changing task states or superseding V therefore does not recursively change the evidence it summarizes. Changing a contract, applicable choice, plan or criterion invalidates live E bindings. Superseded V retains its old outcome and references but no longer requires current criterion membership or current E support. This permits an explicitly revised plan to retain historical rejected or obsolete requirements.
42	
43	A done task needs all prerequisite tasks done, at least one F, exactly one nominated X per F, and a current passing V for every Q on every nominee. Mechanical success alone cannot satisfy visual or engine criteria. Older rejected candidates remain recorded and do not prevent selecting a later candidate, but no unreviewed replacement inherits their proof.
44	
45	## Publication, amendment and resumption
46	
47	All PX1 concurrency, path confinement, immutable E and history publication guarantees remain. V fields are immutable after publication except one-way `ob=+`; correcting a verdict adds a new V ID. A newly introduced V cannot already be superseded: it must first pass current validation and be published, then a later revision may supersede it. Existing IDs cannot disappear. A store rejects format changes during commit. Existing PX1 stores are not automatically upgraded because old state does not identify confirmed choices or required acceptance. Start a new explicitly authored PX2 project when these operations are needed; preserve the old project as its own source/history.
48	
49	For each newly published pass/fail V, the planned F and its complete semantic scope, including Q and C/choices, must already exist unchanged in the immediately preceding saved state. Save planning/criterion changes before collecting and publishing results. Initial PX2 publication cannot contain pass/fail V. Unavailable observations do not claim evaluation and are exempt from this ordering rule. This establishes recorded ordering between a plan and its verdict; it cannot independently attest when a person actually inspected an image.
50	
51	A done task must reopen when it or its relevant dependency closure changes. PX2 closure does not traverse through P: an unrelated intake choice or project display name does not reopen an accepted sample. Link actual semantic dependencies through its input/output contracts, choices, criteria, sources and decisions. Changing one of those dependencies requires reopening and superseding stale E/V before new evaluation. History remains available for cold resumption.
52	
53	## Operational boundaries
54	
55	Use `intake`, `decode`, `encode`, `validate`, `commit`, `workflow`, `ready`, `context` and `impact` through the selected runner; MCP adds `pixl_intake` and `pixl_workflow`. `context` retains PX2 format and complete references. Mutable state and evidence live in the art project, outside installed resources. Generic encode/commit can author the declared records; they do not perform inspection or grant approval.
56	
57	This version supplies the local intake/sample lifecycle. The original platform prepare/job tools remain stateless local operations. Real PixelLab execution, actual visual judgments, destination-engine verification and model performance require their own observed evidence.
58	
59	## Durable provider jobs (registry 2.1.0 extension)
60	
61	J opts into durable history by supplying `jr` (current journal report X), `op` (nonempty distinct F outputs) and `xs` (all imported X candidates in event order, initially empty). J.xs preserves typed dependency closure for focused retrieval; these are not task nominations. Existing J without these fields retains its earlier semantics. A published legacy J cannot acquire this extension, and a durable J cannot shed it. Older PX2 readers reject these additional fields explicitly. PX1 schema and semantics are unchanged.
62	
63	The retained journal uses the version-1 closed JSON contract in [provider-recovery.md](provider-recovery.md). J.tk/tl/ah/si/ri/op must exactly project its task/tool/intent hash/state/remote identity/outputs. J.ev retains ordered local E receipts for every snapshot, starting with prepared intent and adding one snapshot per event. Each non-superseded local passing E binds exactly its immutable journal X and shares its path/hash. The last receipt binds J.jr. Such a pass establishes retention and local consistency; it is not remote, mechanical, visual or engine acceptance.
64	
65	Generic rooted validation replays the journal and every prefix, verifies local bytes and candidate bindings, and rejects invented projections. Publication requires a saved unchanged production plan before new prepared intent, one event per subsequent commit, immutable intent, immutable retained X/E, and unchanged imported candidates. No initial-state job can invent earlier submission history. Preparation and dispatch require satisfied task activation prerequisites and an open/active task. Another nonterminal durable attempt for an overlapping output, or an unjournaled nonterminal job for the task, blocks new preparation/dispatch.
66	
67	The local dispatch claim publishes `unknown` before returning the request to its host. It does not contact a service. Unknown work must be reconciled rather than resubmitted. Caller-supplied observations retain the returned identity and evidence; accepted states require an ID, which cannot change once recorded. Failed and succeeded are terminal except that success may import new candidates. Completion never follows from provider success: imported candidates still require their declared V criteria.
68	
69	Changed request context blocks dispatch but does not erase submitted history or prevent recording observations. Recovery reports list drift and next actions. Imports bind copied local bytes and the original output plan; a changed output plan must be reconciled before import. All operations use expected-hash publication. Unreferenced immutable blobs may remain after a failed commit; state.px is the sole publication authority. Local coordination cannot guarantee exactly-once remote execution or prevent a host from bypassing the procedure.
70	
71	## Family production and delivery (registry 2.2.0 extension)
72	
73	An optional F.bs names the exact X baseline for production or delivery. It is a semantic dependency, unlike the workflow-only T.ip. The baseline must belong to another sample task in the same project; its X is also listed in the consuming task's ip, and its task is a direct dp prerequisite. Open plans may preserve an unaccepted or replaced baseline. Activation/completion requires that exact sample still nominated and its task done. A sample's passing evidence does not automatically accept a family member.
74	
75	F.mb and F.ds together opt a report-kind output of a delivery task into the family operation and require bs. mb is a nonempty distinct ordered list of planned F members; ds is a nonempty distinct list of same-project I destination choices. Members cannot be the family output itself or another family output. They are the baseline's sample output or same-project production outputs sharing that exact bs. All member tasks are direct delivery prerequisites. A family declares at least one continuity Q, with project-specific mode/conditions; engine Q is declared when applicable. All destination choices must be confirmed for delivery activation/completion. Missing/unavailable engine acceptance remains separately represented through Q/V.
76	
77	A family manifest X has xs: baseline X first, then one selected X per member in the saved order (the baseline may also be a delivered member). xs belongs only to family report candidates and is required on every candidate of a family output. These references bind collective acceptance to the actual baseline, selected member identities, their plans/contracts and the destination/criteria scope. Merely listing siblings in T.ip does not supply this semantic proof.
78	
79	The [family delivery manifest contract](family-delivery.md) governs immutable copied files, saved-plan publication, historical membership and current acceptance. Existing family F cannot shed bs/mb/ds, and existing X cannot acquire fabricated snapshot history. Once published, a manifest X and its baseline/member X records are immutable; revisions add new candidate IDs. Changes to underlying contracts/requirements still require the existing supersession/reopening procedure.
80	
81	`family` / `pixl_family` reports baseline eligibility, member and collective acceptance, destination choices, pending provider attempts, saved snapshots and drift. `family-snapshot` / `pixl_family_snapshot` retains selected member bytes and publishes an unaccepted report candidate. It requires an open/active family task, the accepted baseline and all selected members on done tasks, no pending attempts for involved tasks, and the unchanged previously saved family plan. Snapshotting local files is allowed while destination/adoption/collective acceptance remains unresolved; it does not activate, nominate, evaluate or complete the delivery task. Actual artistic continuity and target-engine readiness require their own inspection and evidence.

1	# Candidate inspection artifact and operation contract, version 1
2	
3	This operation operates on saved PX2 candidates using existing X/E/V records. It
4	adds no UDL syntax. The runtime prepares exact local inputs and verifies retained
5	records; callers supply actual observations and criterion judgments. Preparation,
6	measurement, declared review, host viewing evidence and engine execution are distinct.
7	
8	## API and publication
9	
10	`prepare(folder, expected, candidate_id, packet_id, options, root=None)` requires a
11	saved raster X with a matching F owner and C, saved owner task and required Q.
12	`folder` must be a project subdirectory; root defaults to its parent. `expected`
13	is the current canonical state hash. IDs must be valid PIXL identifiers, fresh,
14	and leave enough of the 96-character limit for generated suffixes.
15	
16	Options are closed: required `references` (distinct local S/X IDs; `[]` is explicit),
17	`scale` (integer 2..16), `backgrounds` (nonempty distinct `#RRGGBB` or `checkerboard`);
18	optional `max_side` (64..2048, default 1024), `contexts` (default []). Contexts require
19	explicit `source_frame`. Options impose no universal artistic rules.
20	
21	Each context is one of these closed objects, with a distinct nonempty name and a
22	source ID in the candidate plus explicit references:
23	
24	```json
25	{"name":"walk","kind":"frames","source":"candidate","source_frame":0,
26	 "rects":[[0,0,16,16],[16,0,16,16]],"durations_ms":[100,null],
27	 "pivots":[[8,15],null]}
28	```
29	
30	`source_frame` selects an existing zero-based decoded source frame, even for static
31	images. Rectangles are ordered `[x,y,width,height]`, with nonnegative integer origins,
32	positive dimensions and complete containment in that frame. `durations_ms` and
33	`pivots` have exactly the same length as `rects`; duration entries are positive
34	integer milliseconds or null, pivots are local in-bounds integer `[x,y]` or null.
35	Unknown values remain null. Individual frames and a comparison strip are retained.
36	The strip uses common-pivot alignment only if every pivot is known; otherwise it
37	uses top-left sequential placement. Timing observations do not create animation.
38	
39	```json
40	{"name":"neighborhood","kind":"tiles","source":"candidate","source_frame":0,
41	 "tile_size":[16,16],"grid":[[0,1],[2,3]]}
42	```
43	
44	Tile dimensions are positive integers and must divide the selected source exactly.
45	The nonempty rectangular grid is an array of top-to-bottom rows, with left-to-right
46	entries; each integer is a zero-based row-major source tile index. The declared
47	neighborhood is retained with exact RGBA placement. Every horizontal and vertical
48	neighbor pair reports differing adjacent RGBA edge-pixel counts, never an automatic
49	seam verdict. Boolean and fractional values are not valid integer fields.
50	
51	Public adapters use the same request semantics:
52	
53	```text
54	inspection-prepare STORE CANDIDATE PACKET OPTIONS_JSON --expect HASH --root ROOT
55	inspection-review STORE PACKET REVIEW_ID REVIEW_JSON --expect HASH --root ROOT
56	inspection STATE [PACKET] --root ROOT
57	```
58	
59	CLI JSON arguments are local JSON file paths. MCP root is the configured project
60	root, and the closed tool envelopes are:
61	
62	```json
63	{"tool":"pixl_inspection","arguments":{"path":".pixl/state.px","packet_id":"packet"}}
64	{"tool":"pixl_inspection_prepare","arguments":{"store":".pixl","expect":"HASH","candidate_id":"candidate","packet_id":"packet","options":{"references":[],"scale":8,"backgrounds":["#ffffff"]}}}
65	{"tool":"pixl_inspection_review","arguments":{"store":".pixl","expect":"HASH","packet_id":"packet","review_id":"review","observation":{}}}
66	```
67	
68	`packet_id` is optional only for `pixl_inspection`; the other shown argument keys
69	are required. The review's observation placeholder must be replaced by the complete
70	closed review object described below.
71	
72	Source bytes are captured once and checked against their saved hashes before rendering.
73	Every encoded input, decoded frame, native transparent view, native background view,
74	integer-nearest enlarged background view and requested context is retained. Large views
75	use complete logical crops before enlargement. Packet preparation creates auxiliary
76	X records of kind `reference` for inputs/views and a kind `report` X for its JSON.
77	It changes no nomination, task status, E or V. Publication uses ordinary store CAS;
78	failed publication may leave unreferenced immutable files, as with existing delivery.
79	
80	The closed manifest keys are `version` (integer 1), `kind` (`packet`), `packet`,
81	`candidate`, `output`, `task`, `created_at` (timezone-aware timestamp),
82	`source_state_sha256`, `records`, `rendering`. Each original semantic record has
83	exactly `id`, `kind`, `fields` (lossless codec tagged JSON), `sha256` (record hash).
84	The original semantic proof scope includes the candidate, output, contract, required
85	criteria, explicit references and their semantic dependencies. Mutable task/project
86	workflow records are excluded by `graph.proof_scope`; task identity is retained.
87	
88	`rendering` has exactly `inputs`, `views`, `measurements`, `options`,
89	`context_observations`. Inputs have `source`, `path`, `sha256`, `id`. Views add `id`
90	to the renderer's `path`, `source`, `frame`, `context`, `scale`, `background`, `crop`,
91	`width`, `height`, `sha256`. Paths inside the manifest are relative to its directory.
92	IDs are `PACKET.input.N` and `PACKET.view.N`, zero-based in deterministic render order.
93	Files live at `STORE/inspections/MANIFEST_SHA256/`; the report is `manifest.json`.
94	Views returned to a host have project-relative paths, ready for a root-confined viewer.
95	
96	Packet X metadata is closed and typed: `inspection=packet` (Symbol), `version=1`,
97	`candidate` (Ref), `scope` (ordered original semantic Refs), `files` (ordered retained
98	input then view Refs). Auxiliary X metadata is `inspection=file` (Symbol), `source`
99	(Ref). The loader checks original bodies/hashes, ownership, semantic scope, typed
100	projection, canonical manifest bytes and every retained file. It deterministically
101	re-renders retained inputs to validate all nested rendering metadata and exact bytes.
102	This intentionally trades read cost for a complete closed rendering check.
103	
104	Renderer ceilings apply equally to preparation and retained packet verification:
105	64 MiB/source, 256 MiB aggregate sources, 16,384 decoded pixels/axis, 16,777,216 pixels
106	per frame, 1,024 frames/source, 67,108,864 aggregate decoded pixels, 65,536 exact visible
107	colors/frame, 4,096 views, 2,048 delivered pixels/axis, 64 MiB/encoded view,
108	512 MiB aggregate returned files and 134,217,728 rendered pixels. The 65,537th visible
109	color rejects instead of truncating. Manifests additionally have the codec's 16 MiB
110	limit. Context-specific limits remain those documented by the renderer.
111	
112	Prepare returns store `revision`, `hash`, `state`, plus `packet`, `manifest`, `views`,
113	`measurements`, `criteria`, `files_verified:true`. Criterion entries have `id`, `name`,
114	`check`, `domain`, `mode`, `status`, `verdict`. Missing verdicts are `unperformed`.
115	
116	## Explicit review
117	
118	`review(folder, expected, packet_id, review_id, observation, root=None)` requires
119	fresh IDs and current retained bindings. A done task must first be reopened. The
120	closed observation object requires `reviewer`, `observed_at`, `observations`,
121	`verdicts`, `next_action`, `limitations`. Reviewer names a saved A; observation time
122	must have an explicit UTC offset and lie between preparation and local recording.
123	This is caller-declared time, not an attestation that viewing happened.
124	
125	Each observation has exactly `view`, `delivered_size`, `note`. View IDs must belong to
126	this packet and cannot repeat. Dimensions are two positive integers or null. Null
127	means the host has not established dimensions; never copy file dimensions into an
128	unknown host delivery. Notes and next action are nonempty text; limitations is a
129	list of nonempty strings, which may be empty.
130	
131	Each verdict has exactly `criterion`, `status`, `reason`, `supersedes`. Criteria must
132	be distinct and required by this packet's original output. Reasons are nonempty.
133	Local criteria accept pass/fail; engine-domain or live-mode criteria accept only
134	unavailable, without E. Visual/continuity or visual-mode failures need at least one
135	observed candidate-source view; viewing only references cannot establish a candidate
136	failure. Visual/continuity or visual-mode passes require every prepared view, including reference and
137	context native/enlarged variants, observed at its prepared dimensions. Unknown or
138	resized deliveries cannot satisfy complete coverage. This verifies declaration
139	consistency; actual viewing transcripts remain separate evidence. Mechanical criteria
140	with local evidence mode do not require image-view coverage. Their verdicts still
141	require an explicit caller judgment against the saved criterion; measurements are
